title: Willful Patent Infringement: How to Prove or Defend It
summary: A patent litigator’s evidence guide to willfulness: prove or rebut knowledge, deliberate conduct, and § 284 enhanced damages after Halo.
body_markdown:
Willful patent infringement under U.S. law involves three separate decisions: underlying infringement, factual willfulness, and discretionary enhanced damages under 35 U.S.C. § 284 ([statutory text](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=%28title%3A35+section%3A284+edition%3Aprelim%29) ) after *Halo* . The patent owner must first establish infringement, then prove by a preponderance that the accused infringer knew of the asserted patent and deliberately or intentionally infringed it. In a jury case, the jury decides that factual issue. The court separately may award no enhancement or up to three times compensatory damages. Knowledge or notice alone does not trigger trebling. Our guide to[software patent infringement](https://www.tryandai.com/blog/software-patent-infringement) addresses claim-to-product proof. This is educational material, not legal advice.


## The three questions that should not be conflated


Willfulness is not another route to proving infringement, and a willfulness verdict is not an enhanced-damages award. The sequence matters because each question has different evidence, a different decision-maker, and a different legal consequence.


Question What must be decided Decision-maker and consequence


**1. Underlying infringement** Did the accused product or process meet every limitation of an asserted claim during the relevant period? The jury or court decides liability. Without infringement, there is no willful infringement to enhance.


**2. Factual willfulness** Did the accused infringer know of the asserted patent and deliberately or intentionally infringe it? In a jury case, the jury decides this fact under the preponderance standard. A finding permits the court to consider enhancement; it does not set a multiplier.


**3. Enhanced damages** Does the whole record show misconduct sufficiently egregious to warrant a punitive increase, and if so, how much? The judge exercises § 284 discretion. The range is no enhancement through a maximum of three times compensatory damages.


**Binding, Supreme Court.** *Halo Electronics, Inc. v. Pulse Electronics, Inc.* ([Supreme Court opinion](https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/boundvolumes/579BV.pdf) ), 579 U.S. 93, 103–08 (2016), rejected *In re Seagate Technology, LLC* ’s rigid objective-recklessness threshold and clear-and-convincing burden. *Halo* restored the ordinary preponderance standard and focused culpability on the actor’s knowledge when it acted. The decision still reserves enhanced damages generally for egregious misconduct.


**Binding, Federal Circuit.** *SRI International, Inc. v. Cisco Systems, Inc.* ([Federal Circuit opinion](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/opinions-orders/20-1685.opinion.9-28-2021_1841166.pdf) ), 14 F.4th 1323, 1329–30 (Fed. Cir. 2021), places deliberate or intentional infringement in the factfinder’s willfulness inquiry. Descriptions such as wanton, malicious, and bad-faith belong to the judge’s enhancement analysis. *Eko Brands, LLC v. Adrian Rivera Maynez Enterprises, Inc.* ([Federal Circuit opinion](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/opinions-orders/18-2215.opinion.1-13-2020.pdf) ), 946 F.3d 1367, 1377–78 (Fed. Cir. 2020), likewise separates the jury’s factual role from the judge’s remedial discretion.


## What must the factual willfulness record show?


The record must connect knowledge of the asserted patent to the accused conduct and support an inference of deliberate or intentional infringement. Patent awareness plus proof that a product infringed is insufficient by itself.


**Binding, precedential Federal Circuit.** *Provisur Technologies, Inc. v. Weber, Inc.* ([Federal Circuit opinion](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/opinions-orders/23-1438.OPINION.10-2-2024_2394588.pdf) ), 119 F.4th 948, 955–57 (Fed. Cir. 2024), shows the missing connection. Weber maintained a matrix that tracked the asserted patents and rated their general business relevance. The matrix did not identify how those patents related to any Weber product. With no evidence that Weber knew of its alleged infringement or specifically intended to infringe, the Federal Circuit reversed the willfulness finding.


A stronger record ties a particular patent, claim, product, recipient, and date together. Depending on the full record, probative themes can include:


- a delivered notice letter or claim chart that identifies the patent and accused product;
- internal discussion that compares a claim or patent to the product;
- copying, competitor monitoring, or reverse engineering connected to the accused feature;
- a decision to continue the accused conduct after a contemporaneous technical assessment;
- a product-specific redesign, design-around, remediation, or sales decision; and
- evidence that specific patent information reached a decision-maker but was withheld from the people responsible for the product.


These facts create no presumption. Their weight depends on who knew what, when they knew it, what decision they controlled, and whether the source can be authenticated. Broad portfolio awareness and market competition may establish context while leaving the required product-specific inference unsupported.


Timing also limits hindsight. **Binding, Supreme Court and Federal Circuit.** *Halo* measures culpability against the actor’s knowledge at the time of the challenged conduct; a defense first developed for litigation does not itself show what the actor knew earlier. *Pavo Solutions LLC v. Kingston Technology Co.* ([Federal Circuit opinion](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/opinions-orders/21-1834.OPINION.6-3-2022_1960213.pdf) ) applies the same timing principle to its record: the Board’s later inaction was irrelevant to Kingston’s intent at the time of the challenged conduct. Later events likewise cannot retroactively establish an earlier mental state.


Willful blindness is analytically separate. *Global-Tech Appliances, Inc. v. SEB S.A.* ([Supreme Court opinion](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/USREPORTS-563/USREPORTS-563-754) ), 563 U.S. 754, 769–71 (2011), concerned induced infringement under § 271(b). Its two-part inquiry asks whether the defendant subjectively believed there was a high probability of a fact and deliberately avoided learning it. Overlapping evidence may inform a § 284 case, but willful blindness is not a shortcut to factual willfulness.


## Build the evidence record in chronological order


A chronology prevents product proof, state-of-mind proof, and remedy proof from collapsing into one conclusion. It also exposes gaps that a topic-based document collection can hide.


1. **Fix the product and claim facts.** Build the limitation-by-limitation infringement record. Identify product versions, configurations, release dates, sales periods, and sources.
2. **Date the knowledge event.** Connect an issued asserted patent and an accused product to a delivery, meeting, licensing exchange, market event, or other record.
3. **Reconstruct the contemporaneous response.** Identify the business, engineering, product, and decision-making personnel involved. Determine what each knew and did next.
4. **Separate later conduct by date.** Distinguish continued sales, investigation, redesign, design-around, remediation, and litigation events.
5. **Stage factfinding and remedy.** Organize jury-stage willfulness proof separately from evidence offered to the judge on enhancement.


The following matrix maps each issue to the proposition it can actually prove. It is explanatory, not a litigation form.


Issue Plaintiff-side proof themes Defense-side proof themes Nonprivileged sources and likely custodians Timing, provenance, and privilege limit


**Underlying infringement** Claim-to-product comparison, source-linked materials, configuration and version evidence Alternative configuration, version history, unsupported limitation, technical dispute Product, engineering, release, sales, testing, and public-web records Preserve source URL, capture date, original file or version, and witness foundation. An evidence-of-use chart proves product facts, not mental state.


**Notice and patent-specific knowledge** Patent- and product-specific notice, delivery proof, meetings, licensing records, correspondence Wrong recipient, no delivery proof, nonspecific patent or product reference, later knowledge date Legal operations, licensing, executives, sales, mail systems, and correspondence files Keep the § 284 knowledge timeline separate from § 287 marking and actual-notice issues. Those inquiries are not interchangeable.


**Deliberate conduct** Patent/product discussions, copying or reverse engineering, decision to continue, failure to relay specific information Timely technical review, documented product change, contemporaneous noninfringement or invalidity position, no product connection Engineering, product, competitive intelligence, sales, change-control, and decision-maker business records Native files, message metadata, meeting dates, and source chain matter. Section 298 bars an adverse inference from the absence of counsel advice.


**Post-notice conduct** Continued sales combined with product-specific knowledge and conduct evidence Prompt investigation, redesign, design-around, changed release or sales decision Product roadmaps, release records, sales records, change control, testing, and notice-response files A complaint or continued sales alone is not automatically enough. Identify the venue, operative pleading, relevant product version, and dates.


**Enhancement** Duration, concealment, copying, remedial inaction, litigation behavior in context, and other totality evidence; litigation conduct alone does not justify enhancement Closeness of issues, remedial action, good-faith contemporaneous record, limited duration Willfulness record plus remedy-related business and litigation evidence This evidence informs the judge’s discretionary § 284 decision. It is not a second willfulness element for the jury.


Dated native records, a documented collection, preserved URLs and captures, delivery records, version history, and a knowledgeable witness make the evidentiary chain more reviewable. None alone guarantees authentication, admissibility, preservation sufficiency, or a result.

## From pleading through post-verdict enhancement


The three-question separation survives every procedural stage. What changes is the available record and the court’s case-management framework.


### Pleading


**Binding framework; open and venue-dependent application.**[Rule 8](https://www.uscourts.gov/forms-rules/current-rules-practice-procedure/federal-rules-civil-procedure) governs pleading sufficiency, and[Rule 11](https://www.uscourts.gov/forms-rules/current-rules-practice-procedure/federal-rules-civil-procedure) separately governs counsel’s certification that a filing has an appropriate factual and legal basis after a reasonable inquiry. Under the applicable pleading law, a willfulness claim must include nonconclusory facts that plausibly support knowledge of the asserted patent and deliberate or intentional infringement. *Mitutoyo Corp. v. Central Purchasing, LLC* ([Federal Circuit opinion](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/opinions-orders/06-1312.pdf) ), 499 F.3d 1284, 1290 (Fed. Cir. 2007), held that Rule 9(b) did not govern and that the Rule 12(b)(6) procedure followed regional-circuit law. Modern plausibility doctrine requires factual allegations rather than a recited conclusion.


The Federal Circuit has not adopted a nationwide rule that service of the original complaint alone supplies a viable post-suit willfulness theory. District courts disagree. *IOENGINE, LLC v. PayPal Holdings, Inc.* ([district court opinion](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCOURTS-ded-1_18-cv-00452/pdf/USCOURTS-ded-1_18-cv-00452-0.pdf) ) allowed a post-suit willfulness theory at the pleading stage, while *Pact XPP Schweiz AG v. Intel Corp.* , No. 19-1006-JDW, 2023 WL 2631503, at *5 (D. Del. Mar. 24, 2023), reconsideration denied, 2023 WL 3934058 (D. Del. June 9, 2023), rejected complaint-as-the-sole-basis reasoning. Both are District of Delaware applications. This is district-court disagreement, not a circuit split.


### Discovery


**Binding framework; case-specific management.**[Rule 26](https://www.uscourts.gov/forms-rules/current-rules-practice-procedure/federal-rules-civil-procedure) limits discovery to nonprivileged matter that is relevant and proportional. Start with business and technical records that establish the product, knowledge events, response, and decision chronology. Custodians, electronically stored information protocols, and proportionality turn on the claims, sources, venue, and scheduling order.


### Bifurcation and staging


**Open and discretionary.** Rule 42(b), local rules, judge practice, and case-specific prejudice or efficiency concerns may change the sequence of willfulness and damages discovery or trial. *Robert Bosch LLC v. Pylon Manufacturing Corp.* ([Federal Circuit opinion](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/opinions-orders/11-1363.opinion.6-11-2013.1.pdf) ), 719 F.3d 1305, 1308–10 (Fed. Cir. 2013) (en banc), arose from a bifurcated case. It illustrates staging; it does not impose a national sequence.


### Summary judgment and trial


**Binding allocation.** A court can remove willfulness from the jury when the record cannot support the required finding. If a jury decides willfulness, the instruction should ask whether the infringement was deliberate or intentional under the preponderance standard. Under *Eko* , the jury should not decide whether conduct was egregious or worthy of punishment. Those questions belong to the judge.


### Post-verdict remedy


**Binding rule; discretionary application.** The parties may address the whole record and the nonexclusive *Read* considerations in post-verdict briefing. The judge then decides whether to enhance and by how much. *Mentor Graphics Corp. v. EVE-USA, Inc.* ([Federal Circuit opinion](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/opinions-orders/15-1470.opinion.3-14-2017.1.pdf) ), 851 F.3d 1275, 1295–96 (Fed. Cir. 2017), rejects a categorical preliminary-injunction prerequisite for considering post-suit conduct. It does not turn all post-complaint sales into willful infringement.


## Advice of counsel, § 298, and privilege


No, § 298 does not permit an adverse willfulness inference from a party’s failure to obtain or present an opinion of counsel. 35 U.S.C. § 298 ([statutory text](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=%28title%3A35+section%3A298+edition%3Aprelim%29) ) states that neither omission may be used to prove willfulness or intent to induce infringement. **Binding, precedential Federal Circuit.** In *Provisur Technologies, Inc. v. Weber, Inc.* ([Federal Circuit opinion](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/opinions-orders/23-1438.OPINION.10-2-2024_2394588.pdf) ), an attorney-expert testified about the absence of a third-party evaluation, including a freedom-to-operate analysis, without distinguishing legal from nonlegal services. The Federal Circuit held that testimony violated § 298: on that record, a patentee could not use a third-party consultation as a substitute for advice of counsel.


*Official opinion excerpt:[Provisur Technologies, Inc. v. Weber, Inc.](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/opinions-orders/23-1438.OPINION.10-2-2024_2394588.pdf) , No. 23-1438, slip op. at 11 (Fed. Cir. Oct. 2, 2024) (precedential), quoting § 298’s no-adverse-inference rule.*


A party may choose to rely on contemporaneous advice as affirmative state-of-mind evidence. *Omega Patents, LLC v. CalAmp Corp.* ([Federal Circuit opinion](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/opinions-orders/18-1309.opinion.4-8-2019.pdf) ), 920 F.3d 1337, 1353–54 (Fed. Cir. 2019), recognizes its relevance. That evidentiary option creates no duty to obtain an opinion and no general recommendation to disclose one.


Affirmative reliance can put related privileged material at issue. *In re EchoStar Communications Corp.* ([Federal Circuit opinion](https://law.justia.com/cases/federal/appellate-courts/F3/448/1294/637017/) ), 448 F.3d 1294, 1299–1303 (Fed. Cir. 2006), addresses subject-matter waiver when an accused infringer relies on advice. *In re Seagate Technology, LLC* ([Federal Circuit opinion](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/opinions-orders/m830.pdf) ), 497 F.3d 1360, 1372–76 (Fed. Cir. 2007) (en banc), addresses whether that waiver reaches trial counsel. *Halo* displaced *Seagate* ’s substantive willfulness test, not every separate privilege and discovery discussion in the opinion.


The scope of any waiver depends on what the party put at issue and the governing privilege law. Whether to obtain, rely on, disclose, or withhold an opinion is a counsel-and-venue question.


## How the judge may use the Read factors


The familiar *Read* factors organize the enhancement record: copying; investigation and good-faith belief; litigation behavior; size and financial condition; closeness of the case; duration; remedial action; motivation for harm; and concealment. *Read Corp. v. Portec, Inc.* ([Federal Circuit opinion](https://law.justia.com/cases/federal/appellate-courts/F2/970/816/425478/) ), 970 F.2d 816, 827 (Fed. Cir. 1992), identifies these nonexclusive considerations.


Three limits keep that framework in its proper place:


- **It is an organizing tool.** *Presidio Components, Inc. v. American Technical Ceramics Corp.* ([Federal Circuit opinion](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/opinions-orders/16-2607.opinion.11-17-2017.1.pdf) ), 875 F.3d 1369, 1382–83 (Fed. Cir. 2017), confirms that a district court need not mechanically discuss or score every factor.
- **Closeness can still matter.** *Halo* removed objective reasonableness as a threshold defense to willfulness. The judge may still consider the strength and closeness of issues when exercising remedial discretion.
- **Section 285 is separate.** Exceptional-case attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. § 285 ([statutory text](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=%28title%3A35+section%3A285+edition%3Aprelim%29) ) arise under different statutory language. A § 284 enhancement decision does not decide fee eligibility.


A factual willfulness verdict allows enhancement; it does not compel one. After considering the circumstances, the judge may award no increase, a partial multiplier, or up to treble damages.


## What changed in 2024–2026


Recent Federal Circuit decisions sharpen the boundaries without replacing *Halo* .


Development Authority status and narrow takeaway


*Provisur Technologies, Inc. v. Weber, Inc.* ([official case page](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/10-02-2024-23-1438-provisur-technologies-inc-v-weber-inc-opinion-23-1438-opinion-10-2-2024_2394588/) ) (Oct. 2, 2024) **Binding—precedential Federal Circuit.** A patent-tracking matrix and general patent awareness did not establish knowledge of infringement or deliberate or intentional conduct. On the record presented, testimony about the absence of a third-party or freedom-to-operate review violated § 298 because the attorney-expert did not distinguish legal from nonlegal services.


*Halo Electronics, Inc. v. Pulse Electronics, Inc.* , No. 23-1772 ([official case page](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/02-28-2025-23-1772-halo-electronics-inc-v-pulse-electronics-inc-opinion-23-1772-opinion-2-28-2025_2474876/) ) (Feb. 28, 2025) **Nonbinding illustration—nonprecedential Federal Circuit.** This later appeal, distinct from the 2016 Supreme Court case, affirmed a judge’s refusal to enhance after a jury willfulness finding. It illustrates the separate egregiousness inquiry and creates no new binding test.


*Wonderland Switzerland AG v. Evenflo Co.* , No. 23-2043 ([official case page](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/12-17-2025-23-2043-wonderland-switzerland-ag-v-evenflo-company-inc-opinion-23-2043-opinion-12-17-2025_2620462/) ) (Dec. 17, 2025) **Binding—precedential Federal Circuit.** Internal communications that connected a claim, accused product, and request about avoiding the patent were probative beyond bare awareness. The evidentiary ruling was fact-specific, not a universal rule.


*Trustees of Columbia University v. Gen Digital Inc.* , No. 24-1243 ([official case page](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/03-11-2026-24-1243-trustees-of-columbia-university-v-gen-digital-inc-opinion-24-1243-opinion-3-11-2026_2659539/) ) (Mar. 11, 2026) **Binding—precedential Federal Circuit.** On the record presented, notice of a pending application was sufficient to permit a jury to find that the accused infringer should have known of the patent upon issuance; it did not make a pending application automatic notice of an issued patent. The opinion also describes the *Read* factors as an appropriate, optional framework.


*SynQor, Inc. v. Vicor Corp.* , No. 24-1879 ([official case page](https://www.cafc.uscourts.gov/02-13-2026-24-1879-synqor-inc-v-vicor-corporation-opinion-24-1879-opinion-2-13-2026_2647866/) ) (Feb. 13, 2026) **Nonbinding illustration—nonprecedential Federal Circuit.** Willful blindness for indirect infringement and § 284 willfulness remain distinct inquiries. Evidence can overlap, but one finding does not automatically establish the other.


## Frequently asked questions


### Is knowing about a patent enough to make infringement willful?


No. The patent owner must connect knowledge of the asserted patent to the accused conduct and prove deliberate or intentional infringement by a preponderance. *Provisur* shows why general portfolio awareness or a patent matrix can fall short when the evidence does not connect the patent to the accused product and intent.


### Does a complaint automatically make later infringement willful?


No. Post-suit conduct can matter, and *Mentor Graphics* rejects a categorical preliminary-injunction prerequisite. District courts disagree about whether service of the original complaint supplies enough knowledge to plead a later post-suit theory. The factfinder still needs evidence of the required deliberate or intentional conduct.


### Does an accused infringer need an opinion of counsel?


No. Section 298 prohibits using the failure to obtain or present advice of counsel to prove willfulness. If a party affirmatively relies on advice as state-of-mind evidence, the choice can put related privileged material at issue. Waiver scope depends on the reliance and governing law.


### Does a design-around defeat willfulness?


No, not automatically. A timely, product-specific design-around can be relevant to what decision-makers knew and intended, when the change occurred, and whether later product versions continued the accused conduct. Its weight depends on the full contemporaneous record.


### Are willfulness, inducement, and exceptional-case fees the same?


No. Factual willfulness can support a discretionary § 284 damages enhancement. Inducement under § 271(b) has its own knowledge and intent requirements, including a willful-blindness route in appropriate cases. Exceptional-case fees arise separately under § 285. The evidence may overlap, while the legal inquiries remain distinct.


### Does this rule apply to copyright or trademark cases?


No. These standards concern U.S. patent willfulness and enhanced damages under § 284. Copyright and trademark law use different statutes, remedies, and mental-state rules.
